# Introduction to the \(\SIR\) epidemic
The \(\SIR\) epidemic in a population of fixed size runs under the following stochastic dynamics:

 * _Infections_ 
   \(S\to S-1\,, I \to I+1\) occur at rate \(\alpha \, S \, I\);
 * _removals_ 
   \(I \to I-1\,, R \to R+1\)  occur at rate \(\beta \, I\).

The structural parameters of epidemic duration and population size are given by `julia` constants
```{julia}
const duration = 2.0;
const population = 5;
```

```{julia}                                                                              
#| echo: false                                                                          
const MAXPOP = 20                                                                       
if population > MAXPOP                                                                  
    circlabels = ["[$i]" for i in 1:population]                                                                                         
else                                                                                    
    circlabels = [string(Char(codepoint('①') + i - 1)) for i in 1:population]                                                           
end                                                                                     
function timelinelabels(i) round(i) > 0 ? circlabels[Int(round(i))] : "" end ;                                                                             
```   

```{julia}
#| include: false
using EpidemicsCFTP, EpidemicsUtilities, Gadfly, Compose, DataFrames

theme = create_theme(load_theme("config/theme.yml"))

gadfly_theme = Theme(
    panel_fill=theme.blank,
    default_color=theme.default,
    background_color=theme.background,
    major_label_font="CMU Serif",   minor_label_font="CMU Serif",
    minor_label_color=theme.legend, major_label_color=theme.legend,
    major_label_font_size=10pt,     minor_label_font_size=8pt,
    grid_line_width=0mm
)

set_default_plot_size(theme.figwidth, theme.figheight)
```

# Structure of potential infections and removals
Here is an example of a
structure recording times of potential infections (`I`),
perpetuated infections (`P`),
and of potential and conditioned removals (`R` and `C`),
using convenient abbreviations
```{julia}
A = AbstractInfection;
R = Removal;
C = CRemoval;
I = Infection;
P = PInfection;

innovation = Innovation(5,
    A[I(0.11, 2, 3), I(0.2, 2, 5), P(0.4, 1, 2), I(0.5, 2, 5), I(0.6, 2, 4), I(0.85, 3, 4),
        I(0.9, 2, 3), I(1.0, 2, 5), P(1.1, 2, 3), I(1.05, 4, 5), I(1.2, 2, 4), I(1.6, 3, 5),
        I(1.5, 3, 4)],
    R[R(0.3, 5), R(0.42, 3), R(0.7, 3), R(0.55, 3), R(0.95, 5), R(1.4, 2), R(1.55, 1),
        R(1.85, 2)],
    C[C(1.3, 2), C(0.8, 1), C(1.7, 4), C(1.8, 4), C(1.92, 5)]);
```

# Constructing the epidemic
An epidemic can be constructed using a specific `initial` state at time \(0.0\)
(specified as an `SIR` structure) and the structure of `Innovations`.
The epidemic simulation is
computed as part of the construction of an instance
of the  `Evolution` type based on the initial state
and the potential incidents from the `Innovations` structure. 
The function `table_trajectories1` should eventually
find a place in the `EpidemicsUtilities` module.
```{julia}
function table_trajectories1(duration, initial, trajectory)
    t = [state.t for state in trajectory]
    s = [state.s for state in trajectory]
    i = [state.i for state in trajectory]
    r = [state.r for state in trajectory]
    
    push!(t, duration)
    push!(s, s[end])
    push!(i, i[end])
    push!(r, r[end])

    flow = DataFrame(t=t, susceptibles=s, infectives=i, removals=r)
    flow[:, :Population] .= population
    flow[:, :Empty] .= 0
    flow[:, :Epidemic] = flow.removals + flow.infectives
   
    return flow
end ;
```

We now compute the data frame for the epidemic.
```{julia}
initial = SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0)
evolution = Evolution(initial, innovation)

flow = table_trajectories1(duration, initial, evolution.trajectory)
```

# Various plots
The next step is to produce good graphical visualization of
the epidemic, and to explain how one starts to evolve
an \(\SIR\) epidemic in algorithmic time subject to conditioning
on observed removals.

The assumption that all removals are observed is of course
unrealistic. However it is significantly _more_ realistic than assuming
all infections are observed!

## The epidemic curve
First we draw the epidemic curve together with removals and susceptibles trajectories. In this example the epidemic curve peaks at two distinct
locations, as annotated.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-curves
#| fig-cap: "Epidemic curve (with annotated peaks) together with the   \
#|           monotonic curves of numbers of susceptibles and removals."
timelines = layer(flow, yintercept=1:population,
    Geom.hline(style=:dot, size=0.25mm),
    style(default_color=theme.scaffold))
ll0 = layer(flow, x=:t, y=:Empty, Geom.line,
    style(line_width=2theme.trail, default_color=theme.scaffold))
ll1 = layer(flow, x=:t, y=:infectives, Geom.step,
    style(line_width=theme.trail,  default_color=theme.colour(I)))
ll2 = layer(flow, x=:t, y=:removals, Geom.step,
    style(line_style=[:dashdot], line_width=theme.boundary, default_color=theme.colour(R)))
ll3 = layer(flow[flow.susceptibles.!=0, :], x=:t, y=:susceptibles, Geom.step,
    style(line_style=[:dash], line_width=theme.boundary, default_color=theme.scaffold))
fig1 = plot(ll0, ll3, ll2, ll1, timelines,
    Guide.annotation(compose(context(),
     text(1.2, 3.2, "Peak #1"),
     text(1.6, 3.2, "Peak #2"))),
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0, xmax=duration, ymin=0, ymax=population),
    Guide.title("Epidemic curve with removals and susceptibles"),
    Guide.ylabel("Time lines"),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    gadfly_theme)
```

## Boundary based plot
For the coupling construction it is convenient to suppose the
various time lines are infected in increasing index order (Because of the
re-labelling symmetry, this will not affect the statistics of the
evolutions of total numbers of `susceptibles`, `infectives` and `removals`).
This is illustrated in @fig-boundary.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-boundary
#| fig-cap: "Time-evolving boundaries between susceptible, infected, \
#|           and removed portions of the population."
ll4 = layer(flow, x=:t, y=:Epidemic, Geom.step,
    style(line_width=theme.trail, default_color=theme.colour(I)))
ll5 = layer(flow, x=:t, y=:Population, Geom.line,
    style(line_width=theme.trail, default_color=theme.scaffold))
fig2 = plot(ll0, ll4, ll2, ll5, timelines,
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0, xmax=duration, ymin=0, ymax=population),
    Guide.title("Boundaries for the coupling construction"),
    Guide.ylabel("Time lines"),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    gadfly_theme)
```

## Plotting infectious and removed zones
To plot the resulting space-time zones of infection and removal, 
it is necessary to create a dataset
which doubles the data-points by adding a point immediately prior
to each transition.

We need to create a lag and blend this with the original dataframe.
The function to do this, `table_trajectories2`,
should also eventually
find a place in the `EpidemicsUtilities` module.

```{julia}
function table_trajectories2(flow)
    flowlag = deepcopy(flow)
    flowlag.t = circshift(flow.t, (-1)) .- theme.ϵ
    flowlag.t[end] = flowlag.t[end-1]
    return sort!(append!(flow, flowlag))
end ;
```

Here is the resulting data-frame.
```{julia}
flow2 = table_trajectories2(flow)
```
Now we plot the zones of infectivity and removal (@fig-zones).
```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-zones
#| fig-cap: "The epidemic curve together with the infectious and  \
#|           removal zones."
ll6 = layer(flow2, x=:t, ymin=:removals, ymax=:Epidemic, Geom.ribbon,
    alpha=[theme.opacity], style(default_color=theme.colour(I)))
ll7 = layer(flow2, x=:t, ymin=:Empty, ymax=:removals, Geom.ribbon,
    alpha=[2theme.opacity], style(default_color=theme.colour(R)))

fig3 = plot(ll0, ll6, ll7, ll4, ll2, ll5, timelines,
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0, xmax=duration, ymin=0, ymax=population),
    Guide.title("Regions of infectivity and removal"),
    Guide.ylabel("Time lines"),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    gadfly_theme)
```

## Adding incidents to the plot
We now add incidents corresponding to the underlying `innovation`:
see @fig-incidents.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-incidents
#| fig-cap: "Incidents arising from the `Innovation` structure,   \
#|           together with the epidemic curve and infectious and  \
#|           removal zones."
fig4 = plot(ll0, ll6, ll7, ll4, ll2, ll5, timelines,
    Guide.annotation(compose(context(),
        EpidemicsUtilities.draw_elements(innovation, theme=theme))),
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0, xmax=duration, ymin=0, ymax=population),
    Scale.y_continuous(labels=timelinelabels),
    Guide.title("Incidents driving the epidemic"),
    Guide.ylabel("Time lines"),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    gadfly_theme)
```

# Indicating realized incidents
Only some of these incidents are actually realized by the construction:

 * _Infections_ (`I`/\(\mathcal{I}\) and `P`/\(\mathcal{P}\)) must lie inside the infectious zone and reach 
 up to exactly one time line above the infectious zone;
 * _Removals_ (`R`/\(\mathcal{R}\) and 'C'/\(\mathcal{C}\)) must lie inside the infectious zone,

This is illustrated in @fig-realized.
Perpetuated infections (`P`/\(\mathcal{P}\)) will arise as part of the algorithmic time evolution of the entire \(\SIR\) trajectory. Conditioned removals (`R`/\(\mathcal{R}\))
are the _only_ removals which should be realized: if an ordinary removal
(`R`/\(\mathcal{R}\)) is realised then this breaks the conditioning (on all
observed removals) that we have imposed.

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-realized
#| fig-cap: "Realized incidents (emboldened) driving the epidemic:          \
#|           notice that realized removals are exactly those removals lying \
#|           in the infectious zone, while realised infections are exactly  \
#|           those infections reaching from within the infectious zone to   \
#|           just above it."
fig5 = plot(ll0, ll6, ll7, ll4, ll2, ll5, timelines,
    Guide.annotation(compose(context(),
        EpidemicsUtilities.draw_realized_elements(initial, evolution.history, theme=theme),
        EpidemicsUtilities.draw_elements(innovation, theme=theme))),
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0, xmax=duration, ymin=0, ymax=population),
    Scale.y_continuous(labels=timelinelabels),
    Guide.title("Incidents driving the epidemic, realized incidents emboldened"),
    Guide.ylabel("Time lines"),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    gadfly_theme)
```
